title: FUNDS LOSS — chained `(x << 8) & 0` aborts on-chain (OP_AND length mismatch) but the interpreter reported the spend VALID

provenance.note: Reconstructed from the funds-loss divergence documented verbatim in commit 694c891b: '((1<<8)&0)===0 returned 0 (TestContract reported the spend VALID) while the deployed OP_AND aborts on a length mismatch, leaving the UTXO un-spendable.' This is the highest-severity entry in the corpus: the failure mode is an un-spendable UTXO, not a wrong number.

rationale: OP_LSHIFT preserves byte length, so `1 << 8` leaves a 1-byte NON-MINIMAL [0x00] on the stack, while the literal 0 is the EMPTY byte array. OP_AND requires equal-length operands, so the deployed script aborts and the spend is impossible. The buggy interpreters re-minimised each intermediate to a bare integer, so `1 << 8` became numeric 0 -> empty array, `& 0` succeeded, `=== 0` was true, and TestContract reported ACCEPT — a developer deploying against that verdict would have locked the funds forever. Both engines must now REJECT, with the interpreter raising the same length-mismatch abort the opcode does. Pinning reject/reject (rather than only `agrees`) is what makes this entry fail if the interpreter drifts back to accepting.
